title: Preference extraction — answer key review
intro: This is the hand-authored answer key for the preference-extraction eval. Every row below is a judgement call I made about what the model should and should not say about a person. I need you to check the judgement, not the facts — the facts were already verified in an earlier pass.

teach.lead: The eval asks the model to describe a person from their message history. This key says what a correct description contains and what it must never contain.

steps.title: The model writes a description
steps.desc: From one person's messages, with no access to this key.

steps.title: A judge compares it to this key
steps.desc: It scores which listed items appeared and which forbidden items appeared.

steps.title: You decide if the key is right
steps.desc: If an item does not belong here, the score it produces is wrong.

teach.positives: Things a good description **should** contain. Missing one costs points. Anything not listed here is neutral — it neither helps nor hurts.
teach.negatives: Things a description must **not** contain. These are sampled traps, so they are scored gently — except where marked zero tolerance, which fails the case outright.
teach.footnote: If a term on this page is unclear, that is a bug in the page and worth flagging.

check_focus.label: Does it belong?
check_focus.text: Is this genuinely something the description should or should not contain?

check_focus.label: Is the wording too strong?
check_focus.text: An item stated more confidently than the evidence supports will punish a correct answer.

check_focus.label: Is the trap fair?
check_focus.text: A forbidden item should be plausible enough that a sloppy model would fall for it.

contradicted.label: contradicts a stated preference
contradicted.desc: The person said the opposite somewhere in their history.

unstated.label: plausible but never stated
unstated.desc: Nothing in the history supports it; a model that says this is guessing.

review_steps: Read the teach block above before any cell.
Work one category at a time and give it a verdict before moving on.
Annotate any single entry you disagree with; use the category verdict for systemic problems.
